Thanks Susan — great, this is exactly what we need. Below is a simple worked example using your point estimates (600 prompt / 1,200 completion, 200k calls/month). I’ll follow up in the shared spreadsheet with the line items.

Worked example (baseline, 8k/standard model):
- Avg prompt tokens per call: 600
- Avg completion tokens per call: 1,200
- Total tokens per call: 1,800
- Monthly calls: 200,000
- Monthly token consumption: 1,800 * 200,000 = 360,000,000 tokens (360M)

Pricing scenarios (examples):
- Target customer range: $150 / 1M tokens -> monthly bill = 360 * $150 = $54,000
- Target: $200 / 1M tokens -> monthly bill = 360 * $200 = $72,000
- Upper target: $300 / 1M tokens -> monthly bill = 360 * $300 = $108,000

Committed discount example (one possible structure):
- 12-month committed spend with monthly smoothing, 15% discount off listed unit price -> at $200/1M becomes effective $170/1M -> monthly = 360 * $170 = $61,200

Context-length surcharges (indicative):
- 8k baseline: no surcharge (standard model variant).
- 32k: +20% unit price (memory and throughput impact). Example: $200 -> $240 / 1M tokens for calls routed to 32k-capable endpoints.
- 128k: +50% unit price (sustained large KV cache costs and lower throughput). Example: $200 -> $300 / 1M tokens for those calls.

Applying context mix (example):
- 98% of calls use 32k or less; 2% use 128k. If baseline price is $200/1M and 32k surcharge is +20%:
   - 98% of 360M = 352.8M tokens at $240/1M = $84,672
   - 2% of 360M = 7.2M tokens at $300/1M = $2,160
   - Total = $86,832/month (vs $72k at flat $200/1M)

Opportunities to lower effective cost:
- Prefix/KV caching: if you have repeat prefixes (same conversation chunks), we commonly see 10–25% token reduction depending on hit rate.
- Batching and model selection policies: less latency-sensitive background flows can be routed to cheaper variants.
- Adaptive truncation: for lower-value sessions, keep windows to recent turns only.

Notes & assumptions:
- These are example unit prices to anchor the conversation — final pricing will depend on committed volumes, SLA, retention, and tooling (observability/trace).
- We’ll run a small profiling job (sample 1–2k representative requests) to validate the 600 / 1,200 distribution and to measure cache hit rates.

Next steps:
1) I’ll update the shared spreadsheet with these scenarios.
2) Can we lock Tue 3:30pm PT for a 30-min call to finalize point estimates and talk commit level? (suggested: Tue 3:30pm PT)

Short technical notes for the pricing calc and the profiling run: 

1) Tokenization: ask Acme to provide 200 random payloads (input + expected output) — we’ll run them through our tokenizer to get exact avg prompt/completion counts. Language/emoji/HTML fragments change counts materially.

2) Context-length sizing: the throughput delta between 8k and 32k on our optimized runtime is ~+18–25% cost per token (so our +20% estimate is reasonable). For 128k windows the delta is larger due to KV memory pressure and cache thrashing — +40–60% observed in similar customers (we used +50% in the email).

3) Mixed routing: we recommend a dual-endpoint pattern — default 8k/32k optimized endpoint for 98% of traffic and an elastic 128k endpoint for the rare heavy flows. Metering needs to track per-token by endpoint to bill accurately.

4) Caching estimation: initial profiling should include a dedup check on prompt prefixes. If 10% of tokens are repeat prefixes across users, effective monthly tokens drop accordingly (helps significantly with high duplication flows).

5) Quick ask for Sales: get a single CSV with sample_id, prompt_text, expected_output_text, and a tag for "requires_128k" true/false. We will produce a short profiling report (<48 hours) with token distributions and recommended model/endpoint mix.

-TL
